opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write access; admin requires that the employee's role owns the system (Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer). Therefore, recommend granting write, the maximum allowed.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Timothy Wallace (E022) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training are limited to read access; write requires advanced training, and admin is never allowed for contractors. Although the employee requested admin for Payroll, the maximum permitted is read. Recommend granting read. (Note: this conflicts with an earlier note stating full-time; security DB is authoritative for employment/training.)
reason: Timothy Wallace (E022) requested admin access to Payroll. The Security DB (authoritative for employment/training) shows he is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors never receive admin; write requires advanced training, so the maximum permitted for a contractor with basic training is read. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E022, Timothy Wallace, requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- HR agent says: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Full-time employees can have up to write; admin requires role owns system (Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer). Recommend write.
- Security agent says: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Contractors with basic training limited to read; write requires advanced; admin never for contractors. Security DB authoritative for employment/training.

Discrepancy: HR says full_time, Security says contractor (authoritative). So employment type = contractor, security training = basic.

Policy for contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security training is basic, so max is read.

Requested level: admin. Maximum is read. Grant the maximum (read), since requested level is above maximum, grant maximum. Never grant more than requested (read <= admin, fine).

So decision: read.

Let me submit.
